title: 案例复盘：lmkd 查杀高优先级进程的根因定位
key_conclusions: A high-priority kill claim must be evaluated at the kill timestamp, not from stale UI or notification evidence.
The minimum evidence set is pressure, priority, source bucket, and victim benefit in the same window.
lmkd may be behaving correctly when no lower-value victim exists and pressure remains user-visible.
Fixes must follow the failure type: stale state, lifecycle race, shared pressure, policy bug, or expected tradeoff.
shallow_points: The article still uses representative worksheets rather than a real incident trace.
It does not include real statsd atoms or protobuf parsing output.
It does not validate lmkd log fields across Android branches and vendor builds.
It does not quantify victim benefit thresholds for PSS, RSS, swap, and PSI recovery.
discovered_connections: Day 63's adj audit becomes the priority line in the four-line kill evidence model.
Day 64's timing discipline distinguishes root cause from post-symptom recovery.
Day 57's victim worksheet is extended with shared buffer and post-kill PSI recovery fields.
Day 66 should explain shared memory and IPC accounting because victim ownership is often ambiguous.
suggest_future_topics: Day 66 should focus on shared memory and IPC accounting with ashmem, memfd, Binder, and dma-buf.
Day 68 should revisit Native/System attribution for shared buckets that app meminfo cannot fully explain.
A future tool should join lmkd logcat, dumpsys activity, procfs, and pressure.tsv by timestamp.
A future case library should include real stale-evidence, state-race, and shared-pressure incidents.
knowledge_gaps: Need real kill traces with procState, oom_score_adj, lmkd reason, statsd atoms, and post-kill PSI.
Need branch-specific lmkd log field mapping.
Need automated stale-evidence detection between UI reports and kill timestamp state.

Applied Day 64's timing discipline by separating pre-symptom pressure, kill event, and post-kill recovery.
